source.limitations: Moving policy page. Use a pinned policy/version matrix for any real upgrade; this register avoids asserting latest release numbers.

source.title: FACTS Benchmark Suite
source.reported_evidence: Across 15 evaluated models, overall factuality scores were below 70%; the suite separates grounding, search, parametric knowledge and multimodal tasks.
source.limitations: Historical benchmark snapshot, not October 2026 model rankings or enterprise failure prevalence; developer-origin benchmark and automated grading require scrutiny.

source.title: METR task-completion time horizons
source.reported_evidence: Over 100 software-oriented tasks support 50% and 80% task-success horizons; measurements above 16 human-expert hours are marked unreliable.
source.limitations: Page no longer actively updated; clean software/ML/security tasks are not all jobs, and a time horizon is task difficulty rather than autonomous elapsed runtime.

source.title: Mitigating prompt injection in browser use
source.reported_evidence: An adaptive attacker received 100 attempts per environment; the report discusses residual 1% attack success despite improved defenses.
source.limitations: Vendor-specific internal test; not a universal failure probability and not evidence of immunity.

source.title: Agent identity foundations
source.reported_evidence: NIST identifies credential sharing, long-lived tokens and agent delegation/accountability gaps; modern OAuth and workload identity offer existing building blocks.
source.limitations: Qualitative engineering diagnosis, without population prevalence or product qualification.

source.title: Agent identity project comments
source.reported_evidence: More than 600 commenters responded; a DevSecOps environment will be the first implementation use case.
source.limitations: Engagement demonstrates attention, not customer demand or an implemented standard.

source.title: METR productivity experiment redesign
source.reported_evidence: Early-2025 tasks took 19% longer with AI; later results suggested speedups but selection effects and concurrent-agent time measurement made the current effect unreliable.
source.limitations: Do not generalize the old slowdown to current tools or present the biased later estimates as causal proof.

source.title: NIST Generative AI Profile
source.reported_evidence: Identifies confabulation, privacy, harmful bias, human-AI configuration and value-chain risks; supports lifecycle measurement and governance.
source.limitations: Taxonomy and guidance, not an incidence survey, certification or evidence that any mitigation eliminates risk.

source.title: GAO data quality and AI-enabled fraud detection
source.reported_evidence: GAO identifies data quality and skilled-workforce constraints on reliable AI-enabled fraud detection.
source.limitations: Does not quantify the share of losses caused by poor data or establish AI remediation savings.

source.title: Interoperable exchange among US hospitals
source.reported_evidence: In 2023, 43% of non-federal acute-care hospitals routinely engaged in all four exchange domains; 71% had routine outside information access, versus 42% reporting routine clinical use.
source.limitations: Lagged, sector-specific self-report; not current global enterprise interoperability prevalence.

source.title: DCAT 3
source.reported_evidence: Standard metadata supports federated catalog discovery, dataset versions, series and checksums.
source.limitations: A catalog vocabulary does not by itself resolve domain semantics, clean source records or prove correctness.

source.title: Foundation Model Transparency Index 2025
source.reported_evidence: Thirteen developers were assessed on 100 indicators; mean transparency was about 41/100, with major information gaps.
source.limitations: Indicators changed since 2024; disclosure is not equivalent to safety, licensing clearance or model quality.

source.title: GAO AI privacy-related gaps
source.source_type: primary government audit and expert panel
source.reported_evidence: Experts identified persistence, re-identification and secondary-use risks. OMB guidance fully addressed two of ten selected challenges and partially addressed eight.
source.limitations: Federal-guidance audit, not a universal legal determination or an empirical rate of privacy incidents.

source.title: NIST SP 800-226 differential privacy guarantees
source.reported_evidence: Describes differential privacy evaluation and practical hazards when translating mathematical guarantees into systems.
source.limitations: No universal epsilon, error or privacy setting; synthetic data alone is not a privacy guarantee.

source.title: Verizon DBIR 2026
source.reported_evidence: The report attributes 31% of breach entry to vulnerability exploitation and 48% of breaches to third-party involvement.
source.limitations: Contributor dataset and context-specific telemetry are not a random population sample; third-party involvement is broader than compromised dependencies; shadow-AI usage is not a breach rate.

source.title: CISA 2026 SBOM minimum-elements release
source.reported_evidence: CISA and partner agencies released updated SBOM minimum elements to improve software-component and supply-chain visibility.
source.limitations: An SBOM supports inventory and response; its existence does not prove exploitability or security.

source.title: Scattered Spider joint advisory
source.reported_evidence: Documents social engineering and identity-focused intrusions and recommends stronger authentication, help-desk controls and defensive resilience.
source.limitations: Threat-group observations, not an identity-compromise base rate; defensive testing requires permission.

source.title: Eliminating buffer overflow vulnerabilities
source.reported_evidence: CISA calls for memory-safe development, prioritized migration, fuzzing and adversarial product testing against persistent buffer-overflow defects.
source.limitations: No measured business ROI; memory-safe languages do not eliminate logic, dependency or unsafe-interface bugs.

source.title: NIST PQC migration FAQ
source.reported_evidence: NIST describes standardized post-quantum algorithms and interoperability/performance migration testing.
source.limitations: Living resource; no prediction of a cryptographically relevant quantum computer date, nor evidence all products are validated.

source.title: WebAIM Million 2026
source.reported_evidence: 95.9% of one million sampled homepages had detected WCAG failures; mean errors were 56.1/page. Six common categories accounted for 96% of detected errors.
source.limitations: Automatic detection covers only part of accessibility; homepage sampling cannot establish whole-site or legal conformance.

source.title: WebAIM Screen Reader Survey 11
source.reported_evidence: The survey had 1,780 valid responses overall. Among the 1,754 respondents answering the PDF question, 85.6% reported that PDF documents were very or somewhat likely to pose significant accessibility issues. Separately, 70.3% reported using multiple desktop screen readers.
source.limitations: Uncontrolled voluntary sample and self-reported experience; not a representative population prevalence estimate.

source.title: HELM Arabic Enterprise
source.reported_evidence: Six enterprise Arabic tasks assess content, finance and legal QA; the retrieved table includes mean scores of 0.826 for LLM-X Preview and 0.767 for GPT-5.4.
source.limitations: Living snapshot, not language-wide ability or legal/financial suitability; collaboration with Arabic.AI and task weighting matter.

source.title: Generative AI and critical thinking survey
source.reported_evidence: Surveyed 319 knowledge workers about perceived critical thinking effort and confidence when using generative AI.
source.limitations: Self-report and association do not prove cognitive decline, causality or the effectiveness of a proposed interface.

source.title: SCORE research outcomes
source.reported_evidence: About half of assessed claims reproduced precisely, around three-quarters approximately; roughly one-third of reanalyses matched within narrow tolerance; about half replicated with the same significant pattern.
source.limitations: Social/behavioral studies only; distinct substudies have different samples and outcomes. These are not failure rates for all science.

source.title: Leakage in connectome-based machine learning
source.reported_evidence: Compared leaky feature selection, site correction, covariate regression, family leakage and subject leakage against non-leaky evaluation pipelines.
source.limitations: Specific datasets and pipelines; effect size depends on the task and leakage mechanism.

source.title: Verizon DBIR 2026: AI data-loss context
source.reported_evidence: Page 13 distinguishes regular AI use on corporate devices (45%, authorized or not), non-corporate account use (67%), and shadow AI as the third most common non-malicious insider action in its DLP data.
source.limitations: Different denominators and telemetry sources must not be mixed; these figures are not the share of all workers leaking data or breaches caused by AI.

source.title: NIST adversarial ML taxonomy
source.reported_evidence: Distinguishes evasion, poisoning, privacy and abuse attacks and their mitigations across AI lifecycles.
source.limitations: Taxonomy identifies mechanisms, not prevalence or assurance that particular defenses work.

source.title: OPC UA Companion Specifications
source.finding: Companion specifications supply industry information models and semantic interoperability; transport connectivity alone does not establish shared meaning.

source.title: Guide to Operational Technology Security, SP 800-82 Rev. 3
source.finding: OT security must preserve distinctive performance, reliability and safety requirements. Revision 4 was a draft, not the final baseline, at this review date.

source.title: Bundle Protocol Version 7, RFC 9171
source.finding: Delay-tolerant networking explicitly accommodates intermittent connectivity, variable delay and high error rates using store-carry-forward communication.

source.title: FIDO Device Onboard Specifications
source.finding: FDO provides automated device onboarding and late binding to management platforms. The index lists v1.1 and v2.0 as proposed standards; deployment support must be checked.

source.title: A Firmware Update Architecture for Internet of Things, RFC 9019
source.finding: Resource-constrained, long-lived and remotely deployed IoT devices need authenticated firmware updates. The document defines a transport-agnostic update architecture, not a complete fleet product.

source.title: Platform Firmware Resiliency Guidelines, SP 800-193
source.finding: Firmware resilience requires protection, detection and recovery. Corrupted firmware can render a platform inoperable; component resilience does not automatically establish whole-platform resilience.

source.title: Commission guidance to support timely Cyber Resilience Act implementation
source.finding: CRA reporting obligations began 11 September 2026; principal obligations apply from 11 December 2027. Product scope and exceptions require separate assessment.

source.title: OT Backup Quick Start Guide, SP 1339
source.finding: OT backups should be incorporated into change management, tested regularly and reviewed during recovery exercises; possession of a backup is insufficient evidence of recoverability.

source.title: Hardware Bill of Materials Framework for Supply Chain Risk Management
source.publisher: CISA ICT Supply Chain Risk Management Task Force
source.finding: HBOM fields and nesting improve communication between suppliers and purchasers for compliance, security and availability risks. An HBOM is evidence disclosure, not proof of physical authenticity.

source.title: Portable Test and Stimulus Standard 3.0 release
source.finding: PSS captures test intent in one representation for simulation, emulation, FPGA prototypes and post-silicon tests; version 3.0 adds behavioral coverage.

source.title: Metrics and Methodology for Hardware Security Constructs
source.finding: Hardware can contain design and implementation weaknesses. Proposed threat and sensitivity metrics connect weaknesses with attack classes, supporting scoped security-cost trade-off analysis.

source.title: International Roadmap for Devices and Systems 2024 Metrology
source.finding: New materials, devices, integration and process control introduce measurement-science challenges that need characterization methods, tools and infrastructure.

source.title: Digital Twins for Advanced Manufacturing
source.finding: Manufacturing twins face gaps in vocabulary, interoperability, trustworthiness and validation. NIST is developing verification, validation and uncertainty quantification methods and reference implementations.

source.title: Digital Calibration Certificate
source.finding: DCC XML makes calibration data machine-readable, but universal interpretation also requires harmonized terminology and refTypes. Schema validity alone is not semantic sufficiency.

source.title: ULPMark benchmark suite
source.finding: MCU energy varies across sleep, peripheral transfer and active computation. Multiple operational profiles are required instead of a single datasheet power figure.

source.title: New EU rules for durable, energy-efficient and repairable smartphones and tablets
source.finding: Covered devices face battery durability and repair obligations: at least 800 cycles retaining 80% initial capacity and specified spare parts within 5–10 working days for seven years after model sales end.

source.title: Global E-waste Monitor 2024
source.finding: The report estimates 62 billion kg of e-waste in 2022 and a 22.3% documented formal collection and recycling rate. This is not a measurement of any one enterprise fleet.

source.title: Guidelines for Media Sanitization, SP 800-88 Rev. 2
source.finding: Organizations need a sanitization programme with techniques and controls selected for information sensitivity. Rev. 2 supersedes Rev. 1.

source.title: Guidance to support preparations for the Digital Batteries Passport
source.finding: The guidance consolidates 71 data points with category-specific applicability. Passport requirements start 18 February 2027 for each covered EV battery, each covered LMT battery, and each covered industrial battery with capacity above 2 kWh. The capacity threshold qualifies industrial batteries only.

source.title: Empowering SMEs in the age of AI: 2026 OECD D4SME Survey
source.type: nonrepresentative survey of over 2,000 SMEs in 12 OECD countries
source.finding: The survey identifies maintenance costs, time and skills gaps as barriers to effective digital implementation; its sample must not be treated as representative of national SME populations.

source.title: The State of Mobile Internet Connectivity 2026
source.type: industry-body research; official homepage independently retrieved
source.finding: GSMA reports 4.8 billion people using mobile internet and 38% of the population living within coverage but not using it. Researcher direct fetch returned 403; the independent reviewer subsequently retrieved the official homepage and confirmed these figures. Full report methodology was not read.

source.title: Measuring Digital Development: Facts and Figures 2025
source.finding: ITU estimates six billion people online and 2.2 billion offline in 2025, with persistent affordability and quality differences. Its internet-user definition differs from GSMA mobile-subscriber measures.

source.title: When is an interoperability assessment legally required?
source.finding: Certain new or revised binding requirements affecting trans-European digital public services require interoperability assessment; routine maintenance and ordinary equipment procurement usually do not trigger it.

source.title: EPCIS & CBV and EPCIS standard archive
source.finding: EPCIS provides common supply-chain event semantics; 2.x supports sensor observations and certification information. The archive identifies 2.0.1 as current.

source.title: Matter 1.5.1: Enhancing Camera Performance and Expanding Device Flexibility
source.finding: Matter 1.5.1 improves camera multi-stream behavior and installation flexibility. A specification release does not establish support in every device, firmware or controller.

source.title: Digital Product Passport
source.finding: DPPs organize product, component and material information for sustainability, circularity and compliance. Requirements are product- and instrument-specific, not one universal present deadline.
